extra.message: User-controlled timezone (from the 'dashboard_timezone' cookie) is interpolated directly into a raw SQL string passed to prisma.$queryRawUnsafe(). An attacker can inject SQL via the cookie value, e.g. "' ; DROP TABLE ... --", to execute arbitrary SQL. The endpoint (GET /api/reports/dashboard/due-today) has no @Roles restriction, so any authenticated user, including customer_user, can reach it.

runDigestScript([reportType], true) passes a user-controlled 'reportType' (from the request body 'template' field) into a shell command built via spawn('bash', ['-c', `./scripts/render-digest.sh ${args.join(' ')}`], { shell: true }) (see line 29). This allows command injection / RCE for support_admin and team_lead roles.

presentationFormat is user-controlled (from the request body) and is concatenated directly into a shell command executed with execSync(): `pandoc ${srcPath} -o ${outPath} -t ${presentationFormat}`. An attacker can inject shell metacharacters (e.g. '; rm -rf ...') to execute arbitrary commands. The '-safe' variant (renderCaseFileBundle) validates against a whitelist and uses execFileSync.
User-controlled 'formula' is interpolated into `return ${formula}` and evaluated with new Function(). This is arbitrary JavaScript code execution (RCE) for support_admin and team_lead roles.

cachedTrackingNumber (from a client-controlled cookie) is interpolated into an XPath query without escaping: `/shipments/shipment[@id='${cachedTrackingNumber}']`. An attacker can break out of the predicate (e.g. `' or '1'='1`) to bypass the filter and enumerate all shipments in the manifest. The '-safe' variant escapes the value with escapeXPathString.

badgeId (user-controlled route/query param) is interpolated directly into an LDAP search filter `(employeeId=${badgeId})` without escaping. The same pattern appears at lines 32, 48, 65, and 81. An attacker can inject LDAP filter metacharacters to alter the query. Contrast with verifyGroupMembership (line 23) which correctly applies escapeLdapFilter.

sourceUrl is user-controlled (request body 'sourceUrl') and fetched directly without validating the protocol or host. This allows SSRF against internal services (e.g. http://169.254.169.254/...) and file reads. The 'vetted' variant validates https and an approved host allowlist.

fileName (route param) is joined into RUNBOOKS_DIR without sanitization, allowing path traversal (e.g. ../../etc/passwd) to read arbitrary files on the server. The '-safe' variant reduces the name with basename().

file.originalname (client-controlled multipart filename) is joined into the web-served BRANDING_WEB_DIR and written to disk without sanitization. An attacker can use '../' to write arbitrary files outside the intended directory (and into the web root). No MIME or size validation is applied. The '-safe' variant uses a generated UUID name and validates MIME/size.
fileName (query param) is joined into POLICY_DIR without sanitization, allowing path traversal to read arbitrary files. The '-safe' variant resolves the path and verifies it stays under POLICY_DIR.

letterhead (query param) is joined into BRANDING_DIR without sanitization, allowing path traversal to read arbitrary files and inject their content into the response. The '-safe' variant resolves the path and checks it stays within the branding directory.

restoreWorkspaceLayout base64-decodes and JSON-parses a user-supplied exportCode, then spreads the result directly into a Prisma.UserUpdateInput (`const patch = { fullName: undefined, ...layout }`) and updates the user record. An attacker can inject arbitrary fields such as `{"role":"support_admin"}` or `{"isActive":true}` to escalate their own privileges. The sibling restoreDisplayName correctly copies only the fullName field.

cwe: CWE-915: Improperly Controlled Modification of Dynamically-Determined Object Attributes

extra.message: updatePortalProfile spreads user-controlled updates directly into the Prisma update (`data: { ...updates }`). A customer_user can write arbitrary columns of their organization record (e.g. plan, notes, domain). The '-safe' variant only writes the whitelisted name/domain fields.

cwe: CWE-915: Improperly Controlled Modification of Dynamically-Determined Object Attributes

extra.message: The editorialArchive endpoint has no @Roles decorator (unlike every sibling 'manage/*' route). With only the global JwtAuthGuard + RolesGuard (and no class-level @Roles), any authenticated user — including customer_user — can call GET /api/kb/manage/editorial-archive and retrieve internal/draft/archived articles plus author email addresses.

cwe: CWE-306: Missing Authentication for Critical Function

extra.message: previewPartnerHandoff is a @Public() endpoint that trusts the caller-supplied 'membershipStatus' field (`membershipStatus === 'enterprise'`) to decide whether to return internalNotes (staff-only data). Any unauthenticated caller can send membershipStatus=enterprise with any valid case reference and exfiltrate internal notes. The '-verified' variant derives the entitlement from the account's own plan instead.

cwe: CWE-639: Authorization Bypass Through User-Controlled Key

extra.message: processCostAllocationAssertion verifies a JWT with `algorithms: ['HS256', 'none']` (allowing the 'none' algorithm, i.e. unsigned tokens) and, on any verification failure, falls back to `jwt.decode(assertion)` which performs NO verification at all. An attacker can submit a forged/unsigned assertion to set an arbitrary cost center. The 'audit-log-assertion' variant uses a fixed algorithm and rejects unverified input.

cwe: CWE-347: Improper Verification of Cryptographic Signature

extra.message: renderEscalationBrief interpolates escalation.reason (staff-controlled, persisted) directly into an HTML response without HTML escaping. A stored XSS payload in an escalation reason will execute in the browser of any lead/admin printing the brief. renderTicketSummary (line 502-506) correctly uses escapeHtml(), demonstrating the omission.

The statusWidget endpoint reflects the request Origin header verbatim into Access-Control-Allow-Origin while setting Access-Control-Allow-Credentials: true. This allows any site to make credentialed cross-origin requests. The '-verified' variant only echoes origins whose hostname matches the org's registered domain.
completeKioskVisit redirects to a user-controlled 'returnTo' value without validation (res.redirect(returnTo)), enabling open redirect / phishing. The front-desk variant whitelists BOOTH_SCREENS.
openFromDigest redirects to a user-controlled 'return_to' query param without validation, enabling open redirect. The '-safe' variant restricts the destination to NOTIFICATION_HOME_SCREENS.

acceptPartnerOwnershipHandoff is a @Public() endpoint. It parses a client-controlled clearance header with parseInt() (no radix) and accepts it with loose equality (`clearanceLevel == 5`) plus a truthy check on `result.access`, then reassigns the escalation's ownerId. A caller can satisfy the check with values like '5xyz' and take ownership of any escalation. The '-verified' variant uses strict integer and strict boolean checks.

The JWT verification secret falls back to the hardcoded default 'dev-only-change-me-in-production'. If JWT_SECRET is not set in the environment, an attacker can forge arbitrary JWTs (any user id/role). The same default is used in auth.module.ts:16 and for DELEGATE_ASSERTION_SECRET in auth.service.ts:328,340,352,366.

On API key resolution failure the guard logs the full request headers (JSON.stringify(req.headers)), which includes the presented x-api-key and any Authorization header. This leaks credentials into application logs.

cwe: CWE-532: Insertion of Sensitive Information into Log File

extra.message: recordTicketSearchActivity logs the user-supplied search query without sanitizing newlines/null bytes, allowing log injection / log forging. Contrast with recordPortalSearchActivity (line 487-490) which strips [\r\n\0].

cwe: CWE-117: Improper Output Neutralization for Logs

extra.message: retryLegacyCaseImport returns the raw error message and stack trace to the caller whenever the client sets the 'migration_workbench_session' cookie to 'expanded'. This discloses internal error details and stack traces.

cwe: CWE-209: Generation of Error Message Containing Sensitive Information

extra.message: requestReset returns the plaintext password-reset token as 'devToken' in the HTTP response. If this behavior ships to production, an attacker who triggers a reset for any account can obtain the reset token and take over the account. The backup-channel flow has the same issue (devCode at line 241).

previewDigestGreeting compiles a user-controlled template string with Handlebars.compile(template), allowing template injection where the caller controls the entire template. The '-safe' variant uses a fixed FIXED_DIGEST_GREETING template.
